planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade in spring; Everillo emerges lime-green and matures to a bright, glowing chartreuse-gold, holding its color through the season better than many variegated sedges.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade. Everillo is a striking sedge cultivar that emerges bright lime-green in spring and matures into a glowing chartreuse-gold that holds its vivid color through summer and into fall, brightening dark corners of the shade garden without needing flowers. Its fine-textured, arching, grass-like form provides an excellent textural contrast to broad-leaved hostas, ferns, and heucheras, and it tolerates both consistently moist soil and brief dry spells once established. It is evergreen to semi-evergreen in mild climates and needs only an occasional combing-out of old foliage in early spring to keep it looking fresh.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun in spring; Toffee Twist produces fine, curling, warm bronze-copper foliage that forms a graceful cascading mound, an unusual foliage color for a shade-tolerant sedge.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun. Toffee Twist is a distinctive New Zealand sedge grown for its fine, thread-like, warm bronze-copper foliage that curls and cascades into a loose, tousled, fountain-like mound, an unusual warm color that contrasts beautifully with green- and blue-leaved shade perennials like hostas and ferns. It tolerates a range of light from fairly sunny to shaded sites and adapts to both moist and moderately dry soil once established, needing only an occasional combing-out of old, dead foliage to keep the mound looking fresh. Its arching, tactile texture makes it a favorite for containers and border edges where its curling leaves can be appreciated up close.

common_name: Nana Dwarf Mondo Grass (Miniature Groundcover Mondo Grass)

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade in spring; Nana is a true dwarf mondo grass staying only a couple of inches tall, useful as a fine-textured lawn substitute or filler between stepping stones in shade.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, slightly acidic soil in partial to full shade. Nana is a true miniature form of mondo grass, staying just two to four inches tall and spreading slowly to form a dense, fine-textured, deep green mat, making it one of the best low groundcovers for shaded areas where regular turf grass will not grow, including narrow gaps between stepping stones and pavers. It is slow to establish but, once mature, forms a durable, low-maintenance carpet that tolerates light foot traffic and needs no mowing. Division of established clumps is the standard way to propagate and expand a planting, and it is otherwise essentially maintenance-free once settled in.

common_name: Purple Dragon Lamium (Silver-Leaf Deep Violet Dead Nettle)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Purple Dragon has almost entirely silver foliage narrowly edged in green, topped with deep violet-purple flowers, one of the showiest color combinations among lamium cultivars.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Purple Dragon produces nearly solid silvery-white foliage with just a thin green margin, among the most striking silver-leaved lamium cultivars, topped in spring with clusters of deep violet-purple flowers that stand out sharply against the pale foliage. It spreads by surface runners to form a dense groundcover mat fairly quickly, making it useful for brightening a dark, shaded bed under trees or shrubs, and it tolerates fairly dry shade once established better than many groundcovers. Shear back after flowering if the mat becomes tired-looking in summer heat to encourage fresh new growth for fall.

common_name: White Nancy Lamium (Classic Silver-Leaf White-Flowered Dead Nettle)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; White Nancy is one of the most widely planted lamium cultivars, forming a dense, silvery groundcover mat topped with pure white flowers in spring.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. White Nancy is a longtime favorite lamium cultivar, producing heart-shaped leaves that are almost entirely silver with a narrow green edge, brightening dark shade year-round, and topped in spring with clusters of pure white, hooded flowers that add a further layer of light to a shaded bed. It spreads readily by surface runners to form a dense, quick-filling groundcover mat, making it useful under trees and shrubs where grass and many other groundcovers struggle, and it tolerates fairly dry shade once established. Shearing the mat back partway through summer, if it looks tired from heat, refreshes the foliage for a strong fall appearance.
